claims.text: A hybrid framework combining DFT-calibrated machine-learning interatomic potentials, molecular dynamics, and CALPHAD-based thermodynamic integration can predict melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
DFT calculations can calibrate machine-learned interatomic potentials for multi-element high-entropy alloys.
Molecular-dynamics temperature ramps using the calibrated potentials can capture melting transitions.
Post-simulation CALPHAD analysis can extract fusion thermodynamics and liquid-phase properties from the simulation results.
DFT and machine-learning calibration enhances the fidelity of interatomic potentials.
High-fidelity interatomic potentials capture local chemical ordering and atomic interactions relevant to melting.
Machine-learning calibration makes force fields reflect accurate local energetics.
Accurate local energetics enable molecular dynamics to resolve melting events.
The molecular-dynamics simulations can yield latent heat, entropy change, and volume change at melting.
Integration with CALPHAD yields coherent liquid-phase thermodynamic descriptions.
Predicted melting temperatures will be within ±5% of experimental values.
Predicted fusion enthalpies will be within ±5% of experimental values.
Predicted fusion entropies will be within ±5% of experimental values.
The framework will accurately reproduce volume changes at melting.
The framework will accurately reproduce key liquid-phase properties across a broad range of high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The method is most effective when local chemical homogeneity is preserved.
Strong phase segregation may place an alloy outside the calibrated potential's applicability.
Extreme off-stoichiometry may place an alloy outside the calibrated potential's applicability.
Transferability of the machine-learned potentials across substantially different high-entropy-alloy compositions is uncertain.
The pipeline's ability to capture complex phase behavior, including secondary-phase formation, is uncertain.
